subject: [PATCH v3 00/12] nfsd: various delegated timestamp fixes

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern that the SETATTR operation in nfsd_setattr() waits for a delegation return while still holding inode_lock, which can cause a deadlock when the holder sends WRITEs that flush its dirty data before DELEGRETURN. The author agreed to drop inode_lock across the wait and restructure the code in v2.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern that the code does not hold freeze protection for the export's filesystem when updating delegation timestamps in certain situations, such as CB_GETATTR and DELEGRETURN. The author explained that the issue is due to the fact that freeze protection is taken outside inode_lock, but the update of delegation timestamps can still occur while the filesystem is frozen. To fix this, the author added a check for freeze protection in cb_getattr_update_times() and nfsd4_finalize_deleg_timestamps(), and also modified nfsd4_finalize_deleg_timestamps() to wait for a thaw if necessary.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about NFSv4.0 clients being able to get write delegations during grace, which can lead to incomplete GETATTR requests. The author agrees that the same check as in nfs4_open_delegation() should be applied to CLAIM_PREVIOUS and will add this fix.
reviews.raw_body:
nfs4_open_delegation() refuses delegations for NFSv4.0 write opens on
CLAIM_NULL and CLAIM_FH, as its comment explains, but CLAIM_PREVIOUS
skips the check. An NFSv4.0 client reclaiming a write open during grace
can therefore get a write delegation, and NFSD can never complete a
GETATTR that the client sends before DELEGRETURN in the same compound.

Apply the same check to CLAIM_PREVIOUS.

Fixes: 1d3dd1d56ce8 ("NFSD: Enable write delegation support")
Reviewed-by: Aurlien Couderc <aurelien.couderc2002@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c b/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c
index c2c082006d81..f865548c297b 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c
@@ -7542,6 +7542,9 @@ nfs4_open_delegation(struct svc_rqst *rqstp, struct nfsd4_open *open,
 	open->op_recall = false;
 	switch (open->op_claim_type) {
 		case NFS4_OPEN_CLAIM_PREVIOUS:
+			if (open->op_share_access & NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_WRITE &&
+			    clp->cl_minorversion == 0)
+				goto out_no_deleg;
 			if (!cb_up)
 				open->op_recall = true;
 			break;

-- 
2.56.1

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about nfsd_break_deleg_cb() running multiple times per lease, causing cl_delegs_in_recall to be incremented unnecessarily and preventing the client from becoming a courtesy client. The author provided a fix by adding a check for dl_recalled before incrementing the count and setting fi_had_conflict.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about CB_GETATTR replies without SIZE attribute, which caused the waiter to mark the file modified and report an incorrect size. The author added a new bitmap word (ncf_cb_bitmap0) to hold the first word of the reply's bitmap, cleared when the callback is issued. In nfsd4_cb_getattr_done(), a reply without SIZE is now treated as failed, causing the waiter to recall the delegation.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about delegated timestamp handling in SETATTR operations. They acknowledged that the current implementation has issues with EPERM errors for non-owners, incorrect application of ATTR_DELEG, and incomplete reporting of attributes when times are rejected. The author proposed a new approach to decode time_deleg_access and time_deleg_modify into separate fields, apply vetted times with notify_change(ATTR_FORCE), and skip nfsd_setattr() for times-only requests. They also addressed issues with delegated times in CREATE and OPEN operations.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern that the ctime should be updated when any attribute is changed in a delegated atime update, not just mtime. They added a check to set ATTR_CTIME unless the request is a delegated atime-only update and modified the code to move ctime to the current time if vetting of the delegated mtime fails.
reviews.raw_body:
__nfsd_setattr() adds ATTR_CTIME only when ATTR_DELEG is clear, to keep
a delegated atime-only update from moving ctime. But ATTR_DELEG is set
for the whole iattr, so a holder's chmod or chown sent along with a
delegated atime changes the mode or owner without updating ctime.

Add ATTR_CTIME unless the request is a delegated atime-only update. A
delegated mtime whose ctime fails vetting now moves ctime to the current
time instead of leaving ctime alone. Since ctime moves, set dl_setattr
whenever the delegated mtime is applied. Otherwise DELEGRETURN of a
written file restamps the vetted mtime and atime to the current time.

Fixes: f9a348e0de19 ("nfsd: don't set the ctime on delegated atime updates")
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c | 6 +++---
 fs/nfsd/vfs.c      | 8 +++++---
 2 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c b/fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c
index b76320c265e1..f8473d0923b8 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c
@@ -1378,10 +1378,10 @@ vet_deleg_attrs(struct nfsd4_setattr *setattr, struct nfs4_delegation *dp)
 
 	if (setattr->sa_bmval[2] & FATTR4_WORD2_TIME_DELEG_MODIFY) {
 		if (nfsd4_vet_deleg_time(&iattr->ia_mtime, &dp->dl_mtime, &now)) {
+			/* ctime moves too, so DELEGRETURN needn't restamp */
+			dp->dl_setattr = true;
 			iattr->ia_ctime = iattr->ia_mtime;
-			if (nfsd4_vet_deleg_time(&iattr->ia_ctime, &dp->dl_ctime, &now))
-				dp->dl_setattr = true;
-			else
+			if (!nfsd4_vet_deleg_time(&iattr->ia_ctime, &dp->dl_ctime, &now))
 				iattr->ia_valid &= ~(ATTR_CTIME | ATTR_CTIME_SET);
 		} else {
 			iattr->ia_valid &= ~(ATTR_CTIME | ATTR_CTIME_SET |
diff --git a/fs/nfsd/vfs.c b/fs/nfsd/vfs.c
index 4a5674e583cc..7bc251d55c3c 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/vfs.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/vfs.c
@@ -513,10 +513,12 @@ static int __nfsd_setattr(struct dentry *dentry, struct iattr *iap)
 	/*
 	 * If ATTR_DELEG is set, then this is an update from a client that
 	 * holds a delegation. If this is an update for only the atime, the
-	 * ctime should not be changed. If the update contains the mtime
-	 * too, then ATTR_CTIME should already be set.
+	 * ctime should not be changed. Any other attribute change, such as
+	 * a mode or owner change sent along with a delegated atime, must
+	 * update the ctime.
 	 */
-	if (!(iap->ia_valid & ATTR_DELEG))
+	if (!(iap->ia_valid & ATTR_DELEG) ||
+	    (iap->ia_valid & ~(ATTR_DELEG | ATTR_ATIME | ATTR_ATIME_SET)))
 		iap->ia_valid |= ATTR_CTIME;
 
 	return notify_change(&nop_mnt_idmap, dentry, iap, NULL);

-- 
2.56.1

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about granting read delegations to NFSv4.0 clients on CLAIM_PREVIOUS, where the reviewer suggested using OPEN_DELEGATE_READ_ATTRS_DELEG instead of OPEN_DELEGATE_READ. The author explains that exclusive atime authority or merging times from multiple read holders is not supported by NFSD, so they are reverting to using OPEN_DELEGATE_READ and declining attribute delegation as per RFC 9754 section 5.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the potential for a client to be freed while waiting for a GETATTR reply in nfsd4_deleg_getattr_conflict(). They explained that holding a delegation reference alone doesn't keep the client alive and proposed taking an additional client reference under flc_lock. The author also added new functions to handle this case, including nfsd4_get_leased_deleg() and nfsd4_put_leased_deleg(), which will be used in place of nfs4_put_stid().

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch does not address the issue of handling concurrent updates to delegation timestamps, and requested further review.
reviews.raw_body:
Applied to nfsd-testing, thanks!

[01/12] nfsd: don't hold inode_lock while waiting for a delegation in nfsd_setattr()
        commit: 6f51f933294bbcff53fb6c7231f356ae8f1a6467
[02/12] nfsd: take freeze protection before updating delegation timestamps
        commit: e65caea9feff1cce8a270b518e2f4475d6167423
[03/12] nfsd: count a delegation in cl_delegs_in_recall only once
        commit: 266f9a2a591f084149e58e1143374a4d1638a230
[04/12] nfsd: don't grant write delegations to NFSv4.0 clients on CLAIM_PREVIOUS
        commit: d4445ca4e442dc09f4eab20afdafb9d8337860ef
[05/12] nfsd: set ctime when a SETATTR with delegated times changes other attributes
        commit: 1baa7cda2fba4238c193a5262a97f1dfdbf8d099
[06/12] nfsd: pin the client while a GETATTR holds a conflicting delegation
        commit: aa8a7d572d5b9788784038e6a3b7d0bc805e0acf
[07/12] nfsd: recall when a CB_GETATTR reply omits the size
        commit: 2b67daa277211096e5c3dbab460b09df89f74f32
[08/12] nfsd: apply delegated times in a separate times-only setattr
        commit: 74ca288461569f71b86028e72120f8f2fbabff41
[09/12] nfsd: grant a plain read delegation when timestamps are wanted on a read open
        commit: 92a3bf098f0738080cb7869427510364ab6a4d0f
[10/12] nfsd: check fi_had_conflict under deleg_lock before hashing a delegation
        commit: 971425a24fe5961611060799392fff93e8c10804
[11/12] nfsd: take the write delegation grant stat before hashing
        commit: 68c7e0626beace91513d74c0407264a51a127740
[12/12] nfsd: move ctime when CB_GETATTR applies a delegated mtime
        commit: 6f174a0eca19e69a14c34b0ed56b60d484f22fd6

--
Chuck Lever

2026-11-24.patch_summary: This patch series fixes various bugs in the NFSv4 delegated timestamp support, including issues with freeze protection, SETATTR, and CB_GETATTR operations. The patches address problems such as incorrect handling of delegation timestamps, missing ctime updates, and conflicts between GETATTR and delegations. The changes also improve the overall consistency and correctness of the delegated timestamp logic.
